name: Barzillai the Gileadite
charge: Providing the king with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man
summary: When David came to Mahanaim on the run from his son, Shobi, Machir and Barzillai brought beds, basons, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentiles, honey, butter, sheep and cheese of kine, because they said the people were hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness. After the rebellion the aged man of fourscore years came down from Rogelim to conduct the king over Jordan, and declined the king’s table in Jerusalem because at eighty he could no longer taste what he ate nor hear the singing men and women. He sent Chimham in his place; the king kissed him and blessed him, and charged Solomon to keep his sons at the table.
offenseFull: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse, and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David and for the people that were with him to eat, for they said the people were hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness (2 Samuel 17:27-29). The provision answered the actual condition of men who had fled Jerusalem barefoot, and it was brought before the battle in the wood of Ephraim, while the outcome was still open and the hearts of the men of Israel were after Absalom. Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old, and he had provided the king with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man (2 Samuel 19:32). His wealth became provision at the moment the kingdom hung in the balance.

When the king came again, Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and went over Jordan with the king to conduct him over. The king invited him to come over with him and be fed in Jerusalem, and Barzillai asked how long he had to live that he should go up with the king; he was fourscore years old that day, and could no longer discern between good and evil, nor taste what he did eat or drink, nor hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women, so why should his servant be yet a burden to his lord the king? He asked leave to turn back again and die in his own city and be buried by the grave of his father and of his mother, and he offered his servant Chimham to go over with the king, to do to him what should seem good (2 Samuel 19:31-39; 2 Samuel 19:31-37). The Most High set man’s days at a hundred and twenty years (Genesis

6:3), and the days of our years are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore years, and even then their strength is labour and sorrow (Psalms 90:10); the Lord kept cutting the lifespan down because of sin, so that a man of ninety is called very aged in the days of the Maccabees (2 Maccabees 6:24). At eighty Barzillai knew exactly where he stood, and his service had not been a hidden bid for a place at court; he could decline the honour for himself without refusing the king’s kindness toward another.
judgmentFull: The king answered that Chimham should go over with him, and he would do to him what should seem good, and whatsoever Barzillai required of him he would do for him. All the people went over Jordan, and when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place (2 Samuel 19:38-39). The king did not treat the provision of his troubled days as a debt forgotten once the throne was secure. The remembrance went into the next reign: in the charge he gave Solomon at the end of his life, David told him to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite and let them be of those that eat at his table, because so they came to him when he fled because of Absalom his brother (1 Kings 2:7). Barzillai did not move to Jerusalem, and his sons ate at the king’s table there for what their father did when the king was hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.

text.text: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo–debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?

I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?

Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.

Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.
The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.
For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion;
And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
But shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother.
